commits.message:
fix(text): noWrap cuts at the width; "ignore" is the unbounded line (rich-text-b44)

noWrap meant an unbounded line, which is Rich's overflow "ignore". It now
means Rich's no_wrap: no breaks, and a line too wide is cut at the width
by the overflow method. "ignore" joins the one OverflowMethod type that
RenderOptions, RichText, PrintOptions and Column share, and RichText
applies it: no edge, no justify.

Console stops translating "ignore" into noWrap. softWrap sends noWrap and
defaults overflow to "ignore", so softWrap with a named overflow cuts, as
Rich's does: width 12, "aaaa bbbb cccc dddd" with fold prints "aaaa bbbb cc".

fix(console): justify places what print draws as one block (rich-console-c70) (#213)

* fix(console): justify places what print draws as one block, as Rich's Align does (rich-console-c70)

print's justify "left"/"center"/"right" now places each block of a print
(a text run, or any other renderable) as a whole: measured, drawn at that
width, shaped to its widest line, then padded out to the console. Before,
only RichText placed itself, line by line, so a Table or Panel was never
placed and "hi\nhello" centred each line against the full width.

The placement is `placeBlock` in the new src/core/place.ts, so console.ts
reaches it without a third upward edge out of core/. Align is now that
function behind the Renderable interface, and moved from per-line to block
placement with it. Under overflow "ignore" / softWrap the text itself is not
justified, matching Rich's Text.wrap; the block is still placed.

Pinned against Rich 9d8f9a3 bytes in test/core/console.test.ts. The
multi-item text run case is filed separately as rich-console-7yp0.

* fix(console): a text run ending in a break under an empty end gets no extra line (rich-console-c70)

The unplaced close check read the joined text's last character, which
skips an empty trailing segment that splitLines does not: print("a\n",
end="") drew a blank line Rich does not. Closed is now the last
segment ending in a break, which is O(1) and agrees with splitLines by
construction. Also: the justify table's center row names the block,
and placeBlock says why it drops the region height.

* fix(console): a print's text items are joined into one text, as Rich's Text.join does (rich-console-c70, rich-console-7yp0)

TextRun measured the run as one string but drew each item on its own,
so under justify every item was set at the run's width by itself: the
run came out wider than measured and was cropped, and sep="\n" with
justify="right" regressed against master. Measure and render now read
one joined RichText. Each item's own justify/overflow/noWrap/tabSize
stays behind, as in the reference; RichText.append now carries the
appended text's base style, as the reference's append does, so a styled
item keeps its style through the join.

* refactor(console,text): a run is closed by its end; fromFragments is append (rich-console-c70)

closed reads the print's own end rather than re-deriving it from the
drawn output. RichText.fromFragments hand-copied the base-style lift
append now does, and its comment said append did not.

fix(table): draw with Table.style and Column's three styles, as the reference does (rich-table-jph)

Table.style is the base the border style layers over; a column's headerStyle and
footerStyle layer over the table's, and its style sits under the row's rowStyles
entry. The cell's style now covers its padding and the blank lines a short cell
runs out of, which is where the reference puts it. Each case is pinned against
Python Rich 9d8f9a3's bytes.
